confirm.text: Four forms carry an "Unsafe conditions" selection. On three of them the accompanying narrative describes routine work rather than a condition, which is the pattern Kelby identified as a selection habit rather than a reporting one. These are listed so the technicians can confirm what they meant; none of them should be treated as a confirmed unsafe event on the strength of the checkbox alone. Separately, no form filed today selected "Stop work authority utilized" — every form carrying a stop-work item selected "Stop work authority was discussed", which is the routine pre-job item.

"Unsafe conditions" selected, narrative describes routine work: Tyrell Sanders, XTO Flanagan 002, job 37053 — narrative reads "Replacing rod hanger". Tyrell Sanders, XTO Darwin 22 #1, job 37075 — narrative reads "Changed out rubber chains". 1099 Robert Henigan, XTO Flanagan 002, job 37054 — narrative reads "Rod change".

"Stop work authority was discussed" selected (routine, no action): Sanders 37053 and 37075, Henigan 37054, Bobby Galindo 37074, Justin Fontenot 37121 and 37123, Andrew Bailey 37120 and 37122, Bryan Medlin 36973, Michael Jobe 36974, Alexander Clubb 37106_1, Raymundo Solis 37119.
Neither stop-work item selected: Pablo Soto 37073, Trevor McKenzie 37106_2, Humberto Marquez-Salazar 37118.

Raymundo Solis, job 37119, is not the mis-selection pattern. His "Unsafe conditions" selection is backed by a narrative naming unbled valves and the corrective step taken, as set out above. It should be read as a correctly reported condition.

Two further observations on the selections. Sanders and Henigan worked Flanagan 002 together and filed near-identical ten-item observation strings; Sanders selected "Unsafe conditions" and Henigan did not, on the same job on the same day. Sanders also filed the identical ten-item string on both of his jobs today, which suggests the list is being carried forward rather than made fresh. Michael Jobe, who appeared on this list twice on 09/26 and was clear on 11/11, is clear again today.

Both kinds of trailer form and the equipment sections of the H2S daily are photo-based, so a defect visible only in a photograph would not surface in this review. Fire extinguisher inspection and expiration dates, first aid kit dates and 4-gas calibration dates exist only inside the images and not as text, so this report can confirm that a photo was captured and when it was captured, but not what it shows. Where a stale capture date is flagged above, the underlying equipment may well be in order; the finding is that the record does not evidence it for 11/18/2026.

81 of 81 submissions read, plus one 11/17-dated form read and set aside. The job board was available: the 11/18/2026 boards emailed by Blake Walton at 10:14 AM were used, and 47 manned board rows were checked for coverage — 37 on the Permian Basin board and 10 on the ArkLaTex board. This run started at 11:06 PM Central, before the Central day closed, so any form submitted after that time is not in these counts; late-arriving Trailer Readiness Forms are the finding most often resolved that way, and the trailer 139 and 603 readiness gaps above are the most likely to clear overnight.
